videos.script: When one database is not enough, there are three ways to divide it, and they solve three different problems. {{three}} A replica is a second server that follows the first, applying its log a moment later. It takes the reads, and it can take over if the primary dies. {{replica}} But a moment later is still later. You buy a ticket, read the page from the replica, and your ticket is not there yet. {{lag}} Partitioning splits one big table by month, on the same server. A question about June reads June and nothing else, and last January leaves in three milliseconds instead of two hundred. {{partitions}} Sharding puts the rows on different servers, each holding a share. Now writes scale too, and every query has to know where its data lives. {{shards}} Last, you add a third shard and count how many keys have to move. With the simple rule, two thirds of everything. With a ring, one third. {{ring}}
